question_text: What are Jacobson's organs? What is their function?

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.56, VSAQ 119). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. steps.margin_note: Say what kind of organ and where it lies. Two lines.

They lie in the roof of the mouth of snakes and
steps.why: Jacobson's organs are organs of smell placed inside the mouth, so their position explains why the tongue has to carry the scent to them.
common_mistakes: Calling them organs of taste. They are organs of smell.
Giving them to all reptiles. They are found in snakes and in some lizards.
steps.memory_tip: A nose in the roof of the mouth: that is Jacobson's organ.

steps.label: Their function
steps.margin_note: The function needs the tongue in it. Three short lines.

lines.text: Smell: forked tongue brings scent to them

lines: The snake flicks out its bifid (forked) tongue
and collects scent particles from the air.
The tongue is drawn back and placed on these
organs, and the animal smells its prey and its
steps.why: The forked tongue and the paired organ work as one system, so describing the tongue is part of describing the function.
common_mistakes: Writing that the tongue tastes the air. The tongue only carries the particles; the organ smells them.
Leaving the tongue out. The link between the tongue and the organ is the marked point.
steps.memory_tip: Tongue out, particles picked up, tongue in, organ smells. Four steps in one picture.

insider_note: The examiner wants the tongue and the organ connected in one sentence; an answer that only says they help in smelling reads as half learnt.
